props.title: Short Circuit
props.initialSlug: Bolt of lightning. Heart of gold.

sections.content: Short Circuit (1986) sparked a unique moment in 80s robot cinema, landing between the killer machines of The Terminator (1984) and the friendly droids of D.A.R.Y.L. (1985). Steve Guttenberg and Ally Sheedy anchor this story of Number 5, a military robot who gains consciousness after a lightning strike. The film cleverly subverts Cold War anxieties by turning a weapon into a peace-loving, joke-cracking personality. While WarGames (1983) approached AI with dread, Short Circuit opted for optimism and humor.

sections.content: The 1980s witnessed a fascinating shift in robot portrayal, moving from the menacing machines of Westworld (1973) to more sympathetic automatons. Short Circuit shares DNA with E.T. the Extra-Terrestrial (1982) in its "protect the innocent outsider" plot, while laying groundwork for later friendly robot films like WALL-E (2008). Fisher Stevens' problematic portrayal of Ben Jabituya reflects dated cultural sensitivities, but Number 5's journey from weapon to wonder remains compelling. SUBHEAD: The Evolution of Friendly Robots

Number 5's character influenced a wave of lovable machine characters, from The Iron Giant (1999) to Big Hero 6 (2014). The film's balance of slapstick comedy and genuine heart established a template for family-friendly robot stories. While modern films like Chappie (2015) tackle similar themes of machine consciousness with grittier edges, Short Circuit's optimistic take on human-robot relations remains influential.
